openclaw.description: Host OpenClaw's AI agent gateway on Sealos with a browser control panel, token authentication, and persistent storage for configuration and workspaces.

firefox.description: Run a remote Firefox browser on Sealos and use its graphical interface from your own browser through noVNC. Keep the browsing session in a hosted container.

flarum.description: Launch a Flarum community forum on Sealos with discussion threads, moderation tools, persistent storage, and a managed MySQL database.

flowise.description: Build Flowise AI agents and LLM workflows on a visual canvas. Host on Sealos with persistent storage and optional PostgreSQL and object storage.

airbyte.description: Connect databases, APIs, and SaaS tools to a warehouse with Airbyte. Deploy its integration services, PostgreSQL, and object storage on Sealos.

umami.description: Self-host Umami on Sealos to measure website traffic, campaigns, and visitor behavior with privacy-focused analytics and control over your data.

code-server.description: Run VS Code in your browser with code-server on Sealos. Use password-protected HTTPS access and a persistent workspace for code, settings, and files.

postiz.description: Schedule and manage social media publishing with Postiz on Sealos, including PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal, and persistent storage for your publishing workspace.

deeplx.description: Deploy the self-hosted DeeplX translation API on Sealos and connect applications to its HTTP endpoint. This independent gateway integrates with DeepL translation.

glance.description: Bring RSS feeds, weather, videos, and server status into a self-hosted Glance dashboard on Sealos. Customize its pages and widgets through YAML configuration.

kaneo.description: Host Kaneo on Sealos to organize team projects and tasks in your own workspace. Keep project management data under your control with a self-hosted deployment.

localstack.description: Test AWS-compatible APIs with LocalStack on Sealos. Point your SDK or CLI at the hosted gateway to develop S3, SQS, and other cloud integrations.

nocodb.description: Turn relational data into collaborative tables, views, and forms with NocoDB on Sealos. Start with persistent SQLite storage or select managed PostgreSQL.

vllm.description: Serve a compact language model on CPU with vLLM on Sealos. Connect through an OpenAI-compatible HTTPS API and retain downloaded models in a persistent cache.

chatnio.description: Host Chat Nio on Sealos for a shared AI chat interface and model-provider management. Connect your configured AI services through a self-hosted workspace.

drawdb.description: Design database diagrams and generate SQL with drawDB on Sealos. Open the browser editor over HTTPS, then export your work from its local browser storage.

kanboard.description: Organize tasks with Kanboard boards, swimlanes, and work-in-progress limits. Deploy on Sealos with PostgreSQL and persistent storage for data and plugins.

penpot.description: Collaborate on product designs and prototypes with Penpot on Sealos. Deploy its frontend, backend, exporter, PostgreSQL, and Redis services together.

photoprism.description: Host PhotoPrism on Sealos to organize, search, and browse your photo and video library. Use AI-assisted tagging while keeping control of your media collection.

cap.description: Host Cap's video-sharing workspace on Sealos with a media server, MySQL, and object storage. Manage and share recordings created with the Cap desktop app.

chatbot-ui.description: Run Chatbot UI as your own AI chat application on Sealos. Configure model-provider access and give users a dedicated browser interface for conversations.

full-stack-fastapi.description: Start a web application with the Full Stack FastAPI template on Sealos, combining a Python API, PostgreSQL database, and React frontend.

glitchtip.description: Track application errors, performance, and uptime with GlitchTip on Sealos. Connect Sentry-compatible SDKs and investigate failures in a self-hosted dashboard.

grafana-otel.description: Collect application metrics through OpenTelemetry and explore them in Grafana. This Sealos stack includes Prometheus and persistent monitoring data.

librechat.description: Host LibreChat on Sealos for an AI chat workspace with configurable model providers. Bring your own provider credentials and manage conversations in the browser.

nexus.description: Host private packages and proxy upstream repositories with Nexus Repository on Sealos. Keep build artifacts in persistent storage behind an HTTPS endpoint.

opencart.description: Build an OpenCart store on Sealos with managed MySQL, persistent product data, and HTTPS access. Configure administrator credentials during deployment.

phpmyadmin.description: Manage MySQL and MariaDB through phpMyAdmin's browser interface on Sealos. Connect to your database to inspect tables, run queries, and administer data.

pocket-id.description: Run Pocket ID on Sealos to give your applications OpenID Connect sign-in with passkeys. Persist identity data and expose the provider through managed HTTPS.

tailchat.description: Create a self-hosted team messaging workspace with Tailchat on Sealos. Bring group conversations and collaboration into a chat service you operate.

tentix.description: Host Tentix on Sealos for AI-assisted support ticket workflows. Connect a knowledge base and AI provider to help staff draft replies and handle customer requests.

tolgee.description: Manage application translations with a self-hosted Tolgee workspace on Sealos. Bring developers and translators together to maintain localized product content.

calcom.description: Host Cal.com booking pages and team scheduling on Sealos with managed PostgreSQL. Let visitors book available times while you control the scheduling application.

docker-stacks.description: Run Jupyter applications on Sealos with Jupyter Docker Stacks. Open a hosted notebook environment in your browser for interactive code and data analysis.

overleaf.description: Collaborate on LaTeX documents with Overleaf Community Edition on Sealos, including MongoDB, Redis, persistent project storage, and browser-based PDF compilation.

pangolin.description: Deploy Pangolin's identity-aware access control plane on Sealos with persistent configuration. Connect an external Gerbil node for tunnel and egress services.

woocommerce.description: Launch WooCommerce with WordPress on Sealos. The template installs the store plugin and provisions MySQL, persistent site storage, and HTTPS access.

anki-sync-server.description: Host your own Anki sync endpoint on Sealos. Configure compatible Anki clients to synchronize study collections with the server you operate.

chatany.description: Deploy ChatAny's AI chat and image-service interface on Sealos using your provider credentials. Upstream development has stopped; assess maintenance before adoption.

glpi.description: Manage IT assets and service desk requests with GLPI on Sealos, backed by a dedicated MySQL database, persistent storage, and a public HTTPS endpoint.

it-tools.description: Host IT-Tools on Sealos to give your team a browser-based collection of development and IT utilities. Access the tools from a dedicated HTTPS address.

mage-ai.description: Build, schedule, and monitor data pipelines with Mage AI on Sealos. Use a notebook-style editor with PostgreSQL metadata and persistent project files.

node-red.description: Connect devices, APIs, and services in Node-RED's visual flow editor on Sealos. Keep flows and credentials on persistent storage and access the editor over HTTPS.

pdf2zh.description: Translate scientific PDFs with PDFMathTranslate on Sealos while preserving formulas and layout. Use a password-protected WebUI with persistent files and caches.

quay.description: Host an OCI container registry with Project Quay on Sealos. Store images with PostgreSQL, Redis, persistent storage, and automatic initial administrator setup.

eaglercraft-server.description: Host browser-based Minecraft with EaglerCraft on Sealos. Each deployment runs one selected Paper version with an admin console and persistent world storage.

steps: Choose Minecraft 1.12 or 1.8 and set a strong administration password in Deploy now.
Launch the template, open its application card, and sign in to /admin with that password.
Wait for Paper is ready, then use Join game. Players create a profile and register their own in-game password.
deployment.resources: The main game container defaults to a 0.2 vCPU limit, 1 GiB memory limit, and a 1 GiB world volume. Increase capacity as players, map data, and backups grow. These allocations describe the default template; workload requirements vary.
deployment.access: The HTTPS host serves the game at / and the console at /admin; players connect over secure WebSockets. One deployment runs one Paper version. Running both versions requires separate instances and volumes.

n8n.description: Host n8n workflow automation on Sealos with persistent storage and HTTPS webhooks. Choose PostgreSQL and Redis-backed queue mode as your workflows grow.

steps: Choose Deploy now, select your scheduling timezone, and decide whether to enable PostgreSQL.
Enable queue mode for separate workers; the template also provisions PostgreSQL, Redis, and task runners.
Launch the template, open the n8n URL in Canvas, and create the first owner account.
deployment.resources: The n8n editor defaults to a 0.5 vCPU limit, 1 GiB memory limit, and a 1 GiB volume. PostgreSQL and queue mode add database, Redis, worker, and runner resources. Budget for the full selected configuration.
deployment.access: Use the generated HTTPS address for the editor and webhook endpoints. Create credentials for connected services in n8n, then configure and test your first workflow.

grafana.description: Build metrics dashboards with Grafana on Sealos. Keep dashboards and configuration on persistent storage, with SQLite by default and optional managed PostgreSQL.

steps: Choose Deploy now and select SQLite or the optional managed PostgreSQL database.
Launch the template and open the Grafana URL from Canvas.
Sign in as admin with the generated admin_password, update the password when prompted, and connect a data source.
deployment.resources: The Grafana container defaults to a 0.2 vCPU limit, 256 MiB memory limit, and a 1 GiB volume. Optional PostgreSQL adds a 0.5 vCPU limit, 512 MiB memory limit, and its own 1 GiB volume. Adjust capacity for your dashboard workload.
deployment.access: Open Grafana through its generated HTTPS URL. Prometheus, Loki, and other monitoring backends are data sources you connect separately; PostgreSQL stores Grafana application data.
